nodes.summary: Pearl's formula for the probability of necessity (Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, Theorem 3, eq. (54)): under monotonicity, and when `P(x, y) > 0`, `PN = (P(y|x) - P(y|x')) / P(y|x) + (P(y|x') - P(y | do(x'))) / P(x, y)`: the excess risk ratio plus a correction for confounding.
nodes.title: Pearl's formula for the probability of necessity

nodes.summary: The probability of necessity under monotonicity (Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, eq. (53) and Theorem 3): in a model whose variables are all binary (the framework uses one value type), for the treatment `X_i` and the outcome `X_j`, the probability of necessity `PN = P(Y_{x'} = y' | X = x, Y = y)` (with `x, y` = `true` and `x', y'` = `false`) is identified from the observational law and the interventional law of…
nodes.title: The probability of necessity under monotonicity

nodes.summary: If every assignment satisfying `E` has `X_W = w`, then the counterfactual probability given `E` is the observational conditional probability `P(Y | E)` (by consistency).
nodes.title: Evidence that agrees with the antecedent

nodes.summary: `P(Y_{W ← w} ∈ Y) = P(Y | do(X_W = w))`, the law of the submodel.
nodes.title: Without evidence, counterfactuals are interventions

nodes.summary: Counterfactual probability given evidence (Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, §3.4, the computation of `P(Y_{x₁} = y₁ | Y = y₀, X = x₀)` following eq. (28)): the probability that the event `Y` holds for the counterfactual values `X_{W ← w}(u)`, under the law of the disturbances conditioned on the event that the factual values `X(u)` satisfy `E`.
nodes.title: Counterfactual probability given evidence

nodes.summary: Consistency (Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, eq. (36), `X = x ⇒ Y_x = Y`, which §4.1 notes holds automatically under the structural definition): in a unit where `X_W` already equals `w`, forcing `X_W = w` changes nothing: `X_{W ← w}(u) = X(u)`.
nodes.title: Consistency

nodes.summary: Under `do(X_W = w)`, every node of `W` takes its forced value.
nodes.title: Effectiveness

nodes.summary: The unit-level counterfactual (Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, Definition 4, eq. (27)): `X_{W ← w}(u)`, the values the endogenous variables would have taken in the unit with disturbances `u` had `X_W` been `w`, is the solution of the submodel `do(X_W = w)` at `u`.
nodes.title: The unit-level counterfactual

nodes.summary: The disturbances of a submodel are those of the model.
nodes.title: Disturbances of a submodel

nodes.summary: The submodel of the intervention `do(X_W = w)` (Pearl 1995, Definition 2; Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, eq. (7)): the equation of every node `j ∈ W` is replaced by the constant `X j = w j` (so `j` loses its parents), and every other equation is kept.
nodes.title: The submodel of the intervention `do(X_W = w)`

nodes.summary: The causal network of the submodel `do(X_W = w)` has the joint of the mutilated network.
nodes.title: Network of a submodel

nodes.summary: For one node, the law of the submodel of `do(X_k = a)` is the joint of `BayesNet.intervene`; the back-door and front-door adjustments therefore compute it from the law of the model.
nodes.title: Single-node interventions in a structural causal model

nodes.summary: Interventions are truncated factorizations (Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, Corollary 1, eq. (17); Pearl 1995, eq. (5)): the law of the submodel of `do(X_W = w)` is the joint of the network of the model with the arrows into `W` removed and point masses at `w` on `W`.
nodes.title: Interventions are truncated factorizations

nodes.summary: The causal Markov condition (Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, Theorem 1, eq. (15); Pearl and Verma 1991): the law of a Markovian structural causal model factorizes over its causal diagram: it is the joint of `s.toBayesNet`, the product over the nodes of the probability that the node's equation produces its value from the values of its parents.
nodes.title: The causal Markov condition

nodes.summary: The law of the endogenous variables: the image of the product law of the disturbances by the solution map.
nodes.title: Law of a structural causal model

nodes.summary: The values of the parents of node `k` in a full assignment `x`.
nodes.title: Parent values in a structural causal model

nodes.summary: Markovian structural causal model (Pearl 1995, eq. (3); Pearl, *Statistics Surveys* 2009, §3.2): endogenous variables on nodes `0, …, n - 1` in a topological order, each node `k` with parents among the earlier nodes, a disturbance `U k` with law `noise k` (the disturbances are mutually independent), and a structural equation `X k = mech k (X_{pa k}) (U k)`.
nodes.title: Markovian structural causal model

nodes.summary: An assignment is the solution at `u` if and only if it satisfies every structural equation at `u`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the solution

nodes.summary: The solution satisfies the structural equation of every node.
nodes.title: The solution satisfies the structural equations

nodes.summary: The values of the endogenous variables at the disturbance value `u`, computed node by node along the topological order.
nodes.title: Solution of the structural equations

nodes.summary: The weight of `a` under the image of a finite law `w` by `g` is the total weight of the preimage of `a`.
nodes.title: Weights of an image law

nodes.summary: The probability of an event under the law of a model is the mass of the disturbances whose solution lies in it.
nodes.title: Events under the law of a structural causal model

nodes.summary: The law of a structural causal model is a probability distribution.
nodes.title: The law of a structural causal model sums to one

nodes.summary: The total mass of the product law of the disturbances is `1`.
nodes.title: The disturbance law sums to one

nodes.summary: Same parents, and at node `k` the table `z ↦ law of mech k z (U k)`.
nodes.title: The causal Bayesian network of a structural causal model

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
